title: Ecommerce docs
intro: Ecommerce is the whole shop of your own website: catalog, variants and stock, cart and checkout, orders with your own statuses, delivery, couriers, taxes, promotions, loyalty, returns, reviews, wishlist, alerts, reports, catalog SEO and feeds. Every product, order and customer record is kept in your own database, and media in your own storage (Connections). Shoppers sign in with Accounts, payments go through Payments and messages through Notifications, each with its server token pasted into Connections. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, storage, Payments, Notifications and courier keys, so orders placed there are real orders, payments are real payments and messages reach real people. There is no test mode: use your payment gateway's own test keys in Payments if it has them, and delete test orders afterwards.
install: Add the script to every page of your shop, then place each widget where it belongs. A widget renders nothing while its feature is off, the product is stopped or your database is not connected. Every word the widgets show can be changed in Settings → Texts, and their look in Settings → Theme.
attributes: Data attributes of the visitor widgets:

widgets.product_grid: Product listing with filters, sorting, search, page numbers and result totals.
widgets.product_page: The product page blocks: gallery with variant photos, video, variant picker, price and stock, buy box, size guide, FAQs and reviews.
widgets.cart: The cart, checkout and the success page after payment.
widgets.my_orders: The shopper's orders with tracking, invoices and returns.
widgets.alerts_stop: The page an alert message's stop link opens ({stopUrl}): the shopper stops their back-in-stock and price-drop alerts. Make the page at /alerts/unsubscribe/<token> (or the alerts setting stopUrl) and place this widget on it.
widgets.catalog_admin: Products, categories, brands, attributes, stock and media.
widgets.orders_admin: Orders, status moves, shipments, refunds and returns.
widgets.promotions_admin: Coupons, deals, bundles and loyalty points.
widgets.customers_admin: Customers and the blocklist, review moderation, reports and CSV.

jsApi: window.SSEcommerce is ready once the script has loaded. identify(signIn) passes the shopper's Accounts sign-in to the widgets (identify(null) on sign-out). addToCart({ productId, variantId?, quantity? }) adds to the cart; cart.count() and cart.onChange(listener) feed your own header's cart badge. The cart lives in the shopper's browser and is priced by the server on every quote and again when the order is placed.
addToCart: Other scripts on the page add to the cart with a cancelable window event. Chat's product cards use it: when an Ecommerce widget handled the event it calls preventDefault() and opens the cart; otherwise the product's page opens instead.
growthEvents: For Growth (analytics and pixels), the shopper widgets dispatch window events, not cancelable, that Growth's page script listens for; no Growth token is needed. ss:view_item when the product page shows a product, ss:add_to_cart whenever a line is added to the cart (product page, wishlist, addToCart() and the add-to-cart event), ss:begin_checkout the first time the shopper presses Place order, and ss:purchase once the order is placed. The detail is { currency, value, items } (ss:purchase adds orderId and orderNumber, and its value is the order total); each item is { id, variantId, name, price, quantity }, with money in minor units.
signIn: Shoppers browse, fill their cart and see prices as guests. Placing an order, writing a review, keeping a wishlist, setting alerts and claiming a return need an Accounts sign-in: paste your website's Accounts server token into Connections, put the Accounts widgets on your site and pass the sign-in to SSEcommerce.identify(signIn). Ecommerce verifies each sign-in with your Accounts keys and keeps only shop records (orders, loyalty, blocklist) linked to the Accounts user id.
payments: Payment methods are set in Settings → Checkout and payment. Cash on delivery and pay at pickup orders start awaiting confirmation. Online payments and bank transfers go through Payments: paste your website's Payments server token into Connections. The order starts awaiting payment, the shopper pays on Payments' page (bank transfer: your bank details and the proof upload live in Payments, where you confirm receipt), and Ecommerce marks the order paid only after Payments says it was paid for the order's exact amount and currency. A cash on delivery advance is a Payments payment for the advance. A waiting payment is checked again when the order is read (at most every 30 seconds) and before a waiting order is cancelled at the end of its payment window. When an order is cancelled (by you, the shopper or the end of its window), edited, deleted (one or all) or paid by hand (a payment your staff record) before it is paid, its Payments payment is cancelled too, so it can no longer be paid; if the shopper paid just before, the order stays and is marked paid. A delete or a payment by hand waits while Payments cannot be reached, so try again. Money that still reaches Payments after a cancel is recorded on the cancelled order, which shows a refund due; refund it from the order. Refunds of orders paid online are made through Payments; when Payments can only record a refund (bank transfers, some gateways), the order says so and you return the money yourself.
success: After paying, Payments sends the shopper back to the page with the cart widget, with ss_order=<order id> in the address; the cart widget then shows the order's result (paid, waiting or failed). Never treat the return itself as a payment: only the order's status counts.
orderFlow: Orders move through your own statuses (Settings → Orders and messages). You name the statuses, add your own and choose the allowed moves; each status has a role, and the rules of the roles hold whatever the flow, so stock, offer uses, loyalty points and money stay right. Orders start in the one awaiting payment or awaiting confirmation status and nothing moves into those; cancelled and refunded are final. The default flow:

roles.awaiting_payment: Paid online, by bank transfer or with a cash on delivery advance: waits for Payments to confirm; cancelled when the payment window ends.
roles.awaiting_confirmation: Cash on delivery and pay at pickup, and free online or bank-transfer orders (with the checkout setting freeOrderStart: awaiting_payment they start awaiting payment instead, with no time to pay): waits for your staff to confirm.
roles.packed: Packed; serial numbers are captured here with Grades and serials.
roles.shipped: Handed to the courier, with the tracking number and link.
roles.delivered: Delivered: loyalty points are earned, reviews open and return windows start.
roles.cancelled: Final, only before shipping: stock, booked slots, offer uses and redeemed points go back exactly once.
roles.returned_to_origin: The parcel came back: stock goes back and the customer is flagged for cash on delivery.
roles.refunded: Final: the money was returned (through Payments when paid online).

messages: Messages to shoppers and alerts go through Notifications: paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections and edit each template in Notifications (e-mail, SMS or WhatsApp, as you set them up there). Order messages are optional: choose the channels and the statuses that send a message in Settings → Orders and messages. A failed or unconnected send never stops an order. Order and claim messages and staff alerts are sent as required (a shopper's opt-out does not stop them) and kept in your database until Notifications takes them: when it cannot be reached they are tried again on your shop's next visits, for up to a day, never twice. In the order and return templates name is the shopper's name; in the alert templates it is the product's name, with its price and page address, and stopUrl the link that stops that shopper's alerts (do not use {unsubscribeUrl} there: Notifications fills it with its own opt-out from every optional message). Values are words, not codes, from your Texts: paymentMethod is the checkout's name of the method (checkout.method.*), deliveryMethod messages.delivery.* (empty without delivery), cancelReason the note your staff typed with the cancel, else messages.cancelReason.staff, shopper, unpaid or unconfirmed, and a claim's kind and status returns.kind.* and returns.status.*. Every template also gets business. Template keys and their values:
couriers: Couriers are a list in Settings → Couriers: a name and a tracking link template in which {tracking} is replaced by the tracking number (for example https://track.courier.example/?id={tracking}). Staff pick the courier and enter the tracking number when an order ships, and the shopper gets the link.
courierApi: With Courier APIs on, Ecommerce books the shipment with your courier's own API and reads its latest status, using your keys (Connections → Courier API keys). The connection is one generic adapter for any courier: the booking address (Ecommerce posts the JSON body built from your template), the tracking address with {tracking}, your API key, optional extra headers as a JSON object of text values (they may hold {apiKey}; without them the key goes as Authorization: Bearer <key>), the booking body template, and where the tracking number (default trackingNumber) and the status (default status) are in the courier's JSON answers, as dotted paths. In the body template, {number}, {name}, {phone}, {email}, {line1}, {line2}, {city}, {area}, {postalCode}, {country}, {items}, {amount} (decimal), {total} (minor units), {cod} (the decimal to collect, 0 when prepaid), {currency} and {note} are filled in, JSON-escaped. There is nothing to register at the courier: Ecommerce calls the courier, never the other way round.
storage: Product images, downloads and return photos are kept in your own S3-compatible bucket (Connections → Storage). Uploads go from the browser straight to the bucket with a short presigned PUT, so the bucket's CORS must allow PUT (and GET) from your website's origin and from your admin page's origin:
site: Some things must be served from your own domain: the sitemap, product meta tags and structured data, product feeds, llms.txt and your policy pages. Your site fetches them from the API with the server token (never from the browser) and serves them; the snippets below are Next.js route handlers and pages, and any server can do the same with a plain HTTPS request.

siteRoutes.sitemap: The sitemap of your categories, indexable landing and glossary pages and products, with their images (SEO). Above the seo setting sitemapSize addresses (10,000 by default) the answer is a sitemap index whose files are your sitemap address with ?file=categories, ?file=landings, ?file=products-1 and so on; the route below fetches each file from GET /v1/seo/sitemaps/<file>. The index uses the seo setting sitemapUrl (/sitemap.xml by default) as your sitemap address. Add Sitemap: https://<your domain>/sitemap.xml to your robots.txt.
siteRoutes.feedXml: The product feed for shopping and social catalogues (Feeds), as XML.
siteRoutes.llms: llms.txt of your catalog for AI assistants (llms.txt).
siteRoutes.llmsFull: llms-full.txt: every product in stock with its price range, by category, with the grades of each category (llms.txt, with the llms_txt setting full on; 404 otherwise).

productMeta: GET /v1/seo/products/<id or slug> answers { title, description, canonical, image, robots, focusKeyword, jsonLd } for your product page: the meta tags, robots (from the product's noindex and nofollow) and the JSON-LD structured data (a ProductGroup with its variants, as a string safe to put in a script tag). An earlier slug, a slug in other letter case or an archived product sent to its category (retiredUrl) answers { moved: { slug, url } } instead: answer it with a 308 to url. GET /v1/seo/categories/<id or slug> answers the same for a category page (with status coming_soon and robots noindex while it is coming soon).
listing: GET /v1/seo/listing?category=<id or slug>&brand=&grade=&page=&… answers what a listing page (a category, a landing page, or any filtered list) puts in its head and above the grid: { h1, title, description, intro, faqs, canonical, robots, landing, jsonLd } (CollectionPage, ItemList and BreadcrumbList). robots is index only for a category and its pages without other filters and for an indexable landing page; any other filter is noindex, follow, so filtered lists never compete with your category pages. Pass your page's query as it is; an earlier category slug answers { moved } like a product.
policies: GET /v1/policies answers { format, shipping, returns, privacy, terms, warranty } from Settings → Policies, for your own policy pages: empty policies are left out, and {returnDays}, {warrantyDays}, {warrantyMonths} and {business} are filled in. With the checkout setting policyFormat html the texts are HTML cleaned by Ecommerce to p, br, strong, em, u, ul, ol, li, h3, h4, blockquote and links (https or on your site):
chat: Chat's shop tools read your shop through these lookups with your website's Ecommerce server token (paste it into Chat's Connections). They only read. The me/* lookups take the visitor's Accounts sign-in forwarded in the SS-Sign-In header; Ecommerce verifies it with Accounts.
chatRoutes: GET /v1/chat/products?q=<text>&category=<id or slug>&grade=<keys>&minPrice=&maxPrice=&inStock=1&limit=5: search the catalog by words and filters (up to 12 results; with filters the words may be left out)
GET /v1/chat/products/<productId>: one product's details, each variant with its grade, price, stock left and warranty
GET /v1/chat/products/<productId>/quote?variantId=&quantity=1-5&paymentMethod=&city=: the price as the cart prices it, with deals, fees, delivery and the free-delivery threshold
GET /v1/chat/deals?limit=10: active deals with their badge, discount label, colour, banner and hours
GET /v1/chat/products/top?kind=top|new&limit=5: best sellers or new products
GET /v1/chat/me/orders?limit=5 (SS-Sign-In): the visitor's orders with their lines, amount due, tracking note, expected date and dispatch video
GET /v1/chat/me/account (SS-Sign-In): the visitor's first name, loyalty points, city and area
GET /v1/chat/me/shipments (SS-Sign-In): the visitor's shipments with tracking links, notes and expected dates

GET /v1/chat/context?productId= (SS-Sign-In optional): the live store context for AI replies: policies, the 10 newest products with their price per grade, the deals table, the product named and the visitor's first name, city and points, as data and as one text of at most 6,000 characters
customers: A customer is named by their customer id (cus_…, in every customer answer as id; guests have no Accounts user) or a member's Accounts user id, in GET and PATCH /v1/customers/<id>, POST /v1/customers/<id>/seen and the loyalty routes /v1/loyalty/accounts/<id>; a guest's orders, spend and points are theirs by customer id, and a guest who orders with a phone a member's record has orders as that member. Opening an Accounts user who has not ordered yet makes their record (joined when Accounts says), so staff can note or block them; with the checkout setting customerRecords: sign_in a signed-in shopper's record is made at their first visit. GET /v1/customers?userIds=<up to 100 Accounts user ids, comma-separated> gives what a page of your own member list ordered and spent. Accounts shows a shopper's orders in its Orders tab, and Chat in its context panel, with GET /v1/customers/<Accounts user id or customer id>/orders?limit= (server token):
dataRights: Data rights run through Accounts: when a user asks for their data or to be deleted, Accounts calls each product. Ecommerce finds the person's records by Accounts user id, e-mail or phone; an export lists their orders and customer record as the shopper sees them (never unit costs, staff notes or names, or a block and its reason), returns, reviews, wishlist, alerts and loyalty history, and a deletion erases them (with the order messages and staff alerts about them still waiting to be sent) or, where you must keep an order for your accounts, removes the personal details from it. Staff actions in the admin widgets are copied to the Accounts activity log.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket. Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time and asks only for the permissions that user has.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features. Permissions:
kit: In Ecommerce: the lists are order_flow, couriers, delivery_zones, tax_rules, grades and booking_hours (GET and PUT /v1/lists/<list> with { value }, checked like the dashboard's editors). Counts: orders (/v1/orders/count and /counts?by=status|role|paymentMethod|paymentState; role groups the status keys by their role in your order flow), products (by=status|brand|stockState|featured|grade), customers (by=blocked), reviews and returns (by=status), each with the same filters as its list and an /v1/admin/ twin for the admin widgets. An order move or refund and a return claim step made with SS-Actor headers show that staff member's name in the order's or the claim's history, every change shows it in the activity log (with the order number, product name or code as its label), and a refund through Payments names them there too. Every visitor route under /v1/shop/ takes the server token with SS-Sign-In and SS-Visitor-IP. Totals and prices in messages, invoices, packing slips, llms.txt and the Chat lookups (priceText, totalText) follow your Format; order numbers take the year in your business time zone, and report days are days in that time zone.
business: Every product reads your business basics (name, contact, address) from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain. Shop-only details (payment methods, delivery, policies) are Ecommerce settings.
api: Every route answers JSON (feeds, sitemap and llms.txt answer their own formats); errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Amounts are integer minor units of your shop currency. Times are ISO 8601 in UTC. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes that create things or move money take an Idempotency-Key header. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off.

catalogSeo.intro: What the catalog and its SEO can do beyond the basics, each with the feature it needs. Routes are named with the server token; every staff route also has its /v1/admin/ twin for the admin widgets (ticket with catalog.edit), and the catalog admin widget edits every field below.

sections.title: Category and brand status and content
paragraphs: Categories have a status: active, coming_soon (listed with their content, their products hidden) or hidden. Brands are active or hidden, and list the categories they belong to (categoryIds; none = every category). A hidden category or brand hides its products from every shopper read, feed, sitemap, llms.txt and Chat lookup, judged on every read, so switching it back shows them again at once.

Categories also carry an icon (a name of at most 40 characters your website maps to its own icon), content { summary, bullets: [{ text, icon }] } with at most 12 bullets, at most 20 FAQs, a size chart, requiresSerial (true, false or null) and the SEO fields; brands carry the SEO fields and a size chart. Earlier slugs are kept in previousSlugs (read-only).

sections.title: Featured products and staff filters
paragraphs: Products have a featured flag; shop listings take featured=1. The staff product list filters by q, status, kind, category, brand (several, comma-separated), lowStock, featured (1 or 0), stockState (none, out, partial or full; several), hasMedia (1 or 0) and grade (several), and its rows add featured, stockState, grades and mediaCount. Counts take the same filters: /v1/products/count, and /v1/products/counts?by=status, brand, stockState, featured or grade.

sections.title: Rich descriptions and HTML policies
paragraphs: A product's descriptionHtml is cleaned when saved to p, br, strong, em, u, ul, ol, li, h3, h4, blockquote and links with an https or site-relative href (at most 20,000 characters); the plain description is then made from it for search, feeds and AI copy. The product page widget builds the page from that cleaned copy.

Policies (Settings → Policies: delivery, returns, privacy, terms and warranty) are plain text or, with the checkout setting policyFormat html, the same cleaned HTML. {returnDays}, {warrantyDays}, {warrantyMonths} and {business} are filled in when they are read, and empty policies are left out.

sections.title: Product video
paragraphs: A product's video is { kind: 'file', key } (an MP4 or WebM uploaded to your storage like a photo, up to the catalog setting videoMaxBytes, 64 MB by default), { kind: 'youtube', id } (a YouTube id or address), { kind: 'url', url } (https) or null. The shop's product answer gives the file's address and type, or the YouTube embed address, and the product page widget plays it.

sections.title: Size charts
paragraphs: With Size charts on, a chart has a name, a unit (in or cm), at most 12 columns { key, label }, at most 40 rows { size, label, values }, fit advice, notes and active. Products, brands and categories take a sizeChartId: a product page shows the product's chart, else its brand's, else its category's (hideSizeGuide on a product shows none), with an in/cm switch. A chart in use cannot be deleted (409); its answer says where it is used.

sections.title: Photo sizes and variant galleries
paragraphs: There is no image processing on the server. The catalog admin widget's uploader makes thumb, card and detail WebP copies of each photo in the browser, uploads each one to your storage and makes a blur image (a data URI of at most 2 kB); the photo is attached with { key, alt, sizes: { thumb, card, detail }, width, height, blur }. Your own uploader can do the same: every key comes from POST /v1/catalog/uploads for that product.

Variants have their own photos (media: at most 24 per variant and 200 per product, keys of the product's uploads); removing a photo from the product removes it from its variants too. Shop answers give each photo's sizes and each variant's photos, and product cards carry cardImages: the first photo of up to 4 variants that look different (a 2×2 grid).

sections.title: Attributes per category, on variants
paragraphs: An attribute has a slug (made from its name when empty; shop filters are attr.<slug>), the categories it belongs to (none = all), whether it is set on the product or on each variant (on: product or variant; variant attributes are text, number or choice), multiple (several values on one variant), choices { value, label }, visibility (always, or only for some brands, some grades, or when another attribute has a value), how cards show it (none, image or chips), active, and glossary SEO { title, description, body, faqs }.

Variants hold attributes { <attributeId>: value or [values] }, and the product's options are made from them (up to 6 axes; two variants may share options when their grades differ). A product's attribute setup (at most 20 { attributeId, values, customValues, defaultValue }) lists the values it is sold in; Generate adds every missing combination as a variant (at most 250) with the price and stock you give, for one product or up to 100 at once (Variants).

sections.title: Listing filters, page numbers and totals
paragraphs: GET /v1/shop/products filters by q, category, brand and grade (several values, comma-separated), attr.<slug>=a,b, minPrice, maxPrice, inStock, featured=1 and deal=<id or slug>; one active variant must match the price, attributes, grade and stock together. Sorts are newest, price_asc, price_desc, top, sold_asc, rating, name and updated (price ties go to the newest). page (1 to 500) works beside the cursor, and count=1 adds total (exact up to 10,000, else capped is true). Facets carry counts and labels, and cards carry priceMax for price ranges. The catalog setting pageSize goes up to 60.

sections.title: Stock display and sold out
paragraphs: The catalog setting showStock (none, low or always) and lowStockShown (5) decide what shoppers are told: shop answers and Chat lookups carry stockLeft per variant (a number, or null when it is not shown), so the product page can say Only 3 left or 12 in stock. A variant marked soldOut is shown as sold out without changing its stock; POST /v1/products/:id/stock takes soldOut alone or with a stock change.

sections.title: Grades per category
paragraphs: Condition grades (Settings → Grades and serials, or PUT /v1/lists/grades) have a key (lower-case letters, digits, _ and -), a name, a description of up to 1,200 characters, return and warranty days, the categories they are for (none = all), a colour, an inspection video (a file key or a YouTube id), content (summary and bullets), whether they are offered, a condition (new, refurbished or used, used for structured data and feeds instead of the seo setting gradedCondition) and a glossary page's SEO; up to 100 grades. Shop answers give each variant's grade with these details.

sections.title: Serial numbers and the IMEI check
paragraphs: The grades_serials setting serialMode is registered (serial numbers are added to stock first and picked when an order is packed) or typed (typed when an order is packed or later with PATCH /v1/orders/<id> { serials: { <lineId>: ['…'] } }, one per unit, and required before the order moves to a shipped status). serialCheck imei requires 15 digits that pass the IMEI (Luhn) check digit. A category's requiresSerial says whether its products need serial numbers; a product with serialized null follows its categories. Order lines, invoices and the shopper's orders show the serial numbers.

sections.title: Warranty per variant
paragraphs: A variant's warrantyDays (null = the product's, then its grade's, then the returns setting) is kept on the order line when the order is placed; warranty claims use it, and shop answers and invoices show it.

sections.title: Page addresses, slug history and moved pages
paragraphs: The catalog setting productUrl takes {slug} (or {id}), {category} (its first category's slug), {categoryPath} (that category's slugs from the top) and {brand}, for example /{category}/{slug}; categoryUrl takes {slug} or {path}. variantQuery is added to a product's address to open one variant, with {grade} and {attributes} (its slug=value pairs; an attribute with several values names the first), for example grade={grade}&{attributes}. Every link Ecommerce makes follows them: sitemaps, feeds, canonical addresses, structured data, llms.txt, Chat cards, messages and cart lines.

When a product's or category's slug changes, the old one is kept (at most 20 in previousSlugs). Lookups by slug ignore letter case and match old slugs, and then answer { moved: { slug, url } }: your site turns it into a 308 to url (see the product page below). With retiredUrl set to category, an archived product answers moved to its category's page instead of not found.

sections.title: Atlas Search
paragraphs: Basic search matches every word. With the catalog setting search at atlas, shop and Chat searches use Atlas Search on your own database: fuzzy autocomplete on the product name (one typo allowed), text on the tags and summary, and the brands and categories whose names match, filtered on your website and active products and ranked by score (unless the shopper picks a sort); the listing's other filters follow.

Your database must be on MongoDB Atlas. In Atlas, open your cluster → Atlas Search → Create Search Index → JSON Editor, pick your shop's database and the ss_ecommerce_products collection, name the index as the catalog setting searchIndex (ss_ecommerce_products_search by default) and paste this definition:
If the index is missing or the search fails, basic search answers instead, and the dashboard's Overview shows Search index missing until a search works again.

sections.title: Landing pages, listing heads and glossary pages
paragraphs: With Landing pages on (it needs SEO), a landing page is a category, brand and grade combination with its own h1, title, description, introduction and FAQs, one per combination (409 for a second). indexable is auto, yes or no; auto is indexed while at least landingMinProducts (3) of its products are in stock, judged on every read, and answers add url, inStock and indexed. Its address comes from the setting landingUrl ({categoryUrl}?brand={brand}&grade={grade} by default). With AI copy on, POST /v1/landings/<id>/ai-copy suggests its texts.

GET /v1/seo/listing gives the head of any listing your site shows (see Your site serves): robots is index only for a category (and its pages) and an indexable landing page, noindex for any other filter. With the seo setting pagedListings noindex, pages 2, 3 … are noindex, follow with the first page as canonical (index by default: each page its own canonical).

Glossary pages explain an attribute or a grade from its glossary SEO, at the addresses of the settings attributeUrl ({slug}) and gradeUrl ({key}); with an address and a text they are listed in the sitemaps, as are indexable landing pages. An attribute without its own SEO title or text takes the patterns attributeTitle ({name} by default, for example What is {name}?) and attributeDescription (empty by default) with {name}, {unit}, {values} (its first five choices) and {storeName}; with attributeDescription set, every active attribute's page is listed in the sitemaps.

sections.title: SEO fields, structured data, sitemaps, llms-full.txt and IndexNow
paragraphs: Products, categories and brands have seo { title, description, canonicalUrl, ogImage, noindex, nofollow, focusKeyword }, and products at most 20 FAQs (AI copy can suggest them). The seo settings defaultDescription and defaultImage fill pages that have none.

Page titles follow the seo setting titleTemplate ({name} | {business}). Its {name} is a page's own SEO title, else the pattern productTitle or categoryTitle ({name} by default; products take {name}, {brand}, {category} and {storeName}, categories {name}, {category} for the category above and {storeName}, for example {brand} {name} or Shop {name}). Without an SEO description of its own a page takes the pattern productDescription or categoryDescription (empty by default), then its summary and description. brandName is the name {business} and {storeName} stand for (empty: your business name). Empty brackets and separators left over are dropped.

A product's JSON-LD is a ProductGroup with its variants, the condition of each variant's grade, shipping details from your default delivery fee (free for variants priced at or above the free-delivery amount), the return policy, up to 5 reviews and a FAQPage; a category's adds an ItemList of its products.

Above sitemapSize addresses the sitemap is an index of files (categories, landings, products-1, products-2 …) with image entries, served from GET /v1/seo/sitemaps/<file>. With the llms_txt setting full on, GET /v1/llms-full.txt lists every product in stock with its price range and the grades of each category.
With the seo setting indexNowOnSave on and the Growth token pasted in Connections, the address of a product or category is sent to search engines through Growth's IndexNow right after it is saved.

sections.title: Feed options
paragraphs: The feeds settings: itemId (variant ids, or legacy <product>_<variant> ids made from imported records, so Merchant Center keeps your items; legacy also sends the imported product id as item_group_id on every item), googleCategory (sent with every item), gradeLabel (each item's grade name as custom_label_0), itemTitle ({name} - {variant} by default, with {name}, {brand}, {variant} for the options on products with several variants and {options} for the options always), itemDescription (body: the description, else the summary; seo: the SEO description first) and identifierExists (auto: nothing sent; no: identifier_exists no on items without GTIN and MPN). Each item's condition follows its grade, shipping comes from the default delivery fee (0 at or above the free-delivery amount), prices follow your Format with whole units, and variants priced 0 are left out (the catalogues refuse free items).

catalog: Set the shop currency, your product, category and variant page addresses and, if your bucket has a public address or CDN, the media address in Settings → Catalog. Connect your database and storage. Manage products with the catalog admin widget and show them with the product grid and product page widgets.

Categories and brands have a status and content, products a featured flag, rich descriptions, a video, SEO fields and FAQs, and earlier slugs keep working; shop listings filter, count and page, show stock as you choose and can search with Atlas Search (see Catalog and SEO).
variants: Give a product options (for example size and colour), up to 6; each variant has its own price, stock, SKU, photos, warranty and attributes (several values allowed), and the product page shows a variant picker. Generate adds every missing combination of a product's attribute setup (see Catalog and SEO).
multi_location: Keep stock per location (warehouses, shops). Orders take stock from the first location that has it, in the order you set.
grades_serials: Define condition grades in Settings → Grades and serials: per grade its categories, return and warranty days, colour, inspection video, content, condition and glossary page. Serial numbers (such as IMEI) are registered in stock and picked when an order is packed, or typed at packing or later and checked as IMEI if you choose; they appear on invoices, packing slips and the shopper's orders (see Catalog and SEO).
digital_goods: Attach files or licence keys to a product. The shopper gets the download link or key once the order is paid. Files are kept in your storage.
bookings: Sell services in simple slots: each product has a duration, your weekly booking hours are set in Settings → Catalog, and a slot is never booked twice.
checkout: The cart, checkout and success page (cart widget), My orders (my_orders widget) and the orders admin widget. Shoppers must be signed in with Accounts to order; paste the Accounts token. Order statuses and moves, the order number prefix and order messages are in Settings → Orders and messages; couriers and their tracking links in Settings → Couriers; your delivery, returns, privacy, terms and warranty policies, as text or HTML, in Settings → Policies.
cod: Cash on delivery orders start awaiting confirmation. Set the largest order value, an optional advance paid through Payments, the open-order cap per customer, and use the blocklist and the returned-parcel flag in the customers admin widget. Your staff stop and restart cash on delivery for new orders with the setting Offer cash on delivery (enabled), without switching the feature.
delivery_zones: Delivery fees by city or area, free delivery over an amount, delivery days and store pickup, in Settings → Delivery. A shopper's address is matched to the first zone that lists its city or area.
courier_apis: Book shipments and read their status with your courier's API (see Couriers above). Connect the courier keys in Connections.
taxes: Tax rules in Settings → Taxes: a percentage per category or region, and whether your prices include tax.
coupons: Codes for a percentage or fixed amount off, with use limits, dates and conditions, made in the promotions admin widget.
deals: Automatic offers on products, categories or brands, with dates and use limits; shown on product pages and in the cart.
loyalty: Shoppers earn points on delivered orders and redeem them at checkout. Set the earn and redeem rates and the expiry in Settings → Loyalty; staff adjust points in the promotions admin widget.
bundles: Bundles and buy X get Y offers, applied in the cart.
reviews: Ratings and reviews from shoppers whose order was delivered, moderated in the customers admin widget.
wishlist: Signed-in shoppers save products to their wishlist (wishlist widget, and the heart on product pages).
alerts: Back-in-stock and price-drop alerts by e-mail, SMS or WhatsApp through Notifications (templates ecommerce.back_in_stock and ecommerce.price_drop). Paste the Notifications token. With guests on, the product page asks a guest for a phone (with the checkout setting countries, only a phone of those countries, as for guest orders; a member's phone of another country gets no alerts); with targetPrice on, a price-drop alert may name its price. Each message's {stopUrl} opens your stop page (/alerts/unsubscribe/<token>, or the stopUrl setting with {token}): place the alerts_stop widget there. A message that reaches no one (Notifications down or refusing it) is tried again on later uses of your website, 1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes later, then marked failed; a channel that got through is never sent twice.
compare: Shoppers add products to compare and see them side by side (compare widget). The list lives in the shopper's browser.
returns: Return and warranty claims from My orders, within the windows of each item and grade, with photos (kept in your storage). Staff approve, refund (through Payments when the order was paid online) and restock exactly once.
invoices: Invoices and packing slips with the serial numbers on each line, from the orders admin widget and My orders.
csv: Import and export products and stock, and export orders, as CSV in the customers admin widget.
bulk_actions: Change prices, stock, status or category for many products at once, and move many orders at once, in the admin widgets.
reports: Sales by product, category, brand and city, stock age, return rate and margin, in the customers admin widget.
seo: Meta tags, robots and structured data (ProductGroup, ItemList, FAQPage) for products, categories and every listing, the sitemap and its files, default description and image, and IndexNow through Growth, served by your own site from the API (see Your site serves and Catalog and SEO).
feeds: Product feeds (XML and CSV) for shopping and social catalogues, served by your own site from the API, with your item ids, Google product category and grade labels (see Catalog and SEO).
ai_copy: Product descriptions and meta text suggested with your own OpenAI-compatible AI key (Connections → AI provider key: base URL, key and model). Suggestions are shown to staff in the catalog admin widget and never saved automatically.
llms_txt: An llms.txt of your catalog for AI assistants and, with the full setting on, llms-full.txt with every product in stock, served by your own site from the API.
size_charts: Size charts in inches or centimetres with fit advice, linked to products, brands or categories; the product page shows a Size guide (see Catalog and SEO).
landing_pages: Category, brand and grade landing pages with their own copy, indexed only while enough of their products are in stock, and attribute and grade glossary pages, all in the sitemaps (see Catalog and SEO).
